item.title: City-funded primary care centre opens in Langford on Vancouver Island
item.description: The City of Langford on Vancouver Island has officially opened a new primary care centre, with help from municipal funding. It will provide more than 12,000 with a family doctor

item.title: Winnipeg 1st-degree murder trial begins for man accused of killing Mackaylah Gerard-Roussin
item.description: Monday marked an emotional day in a Winnipeg courtroom for the family of Mackaylah Gerard-Roussin, as the murder trial for the man accused of killing her gets underway.

item.title: The Curator: How to stop slush from taking over your house
item.description: From boot brushes to drying racks, here's how to create a winter home entryway that stops snow, slush, and clutter at the door with simple, practical tips for Canadian homes.

item.title: Proposal for massive new data centre in Olds, Alta. has some residents concerned
item.description: If approved, it would be the largest data centre in Canada, by far, but a proposal to build the project in the small Alberta town of Olds, has generated some controversy.

item.title: Indigenous communities back proposed northern Saskatchewan uranium mine
item.description: Indigenous communities are supporting a proposed uranium mine as it seeks final approval from the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission.

item.title: Woman found dead after house fire in central Edmonton, police investigating
item.description: Firefighters responded Monday morning to a blaze at a home near 93 Street and 105 Avenue in the Boyle Street neighbourhood, where EPS were called in after a women was found dead.

item.title: Downtown Calgary office towers to be converted into affordable housing with new grant
item.description: The grant is funded through the Housing Accelerator Fund (HAF), in which future installments may be at risk depending on whether Calgary city council repeals citywide rezoning.

item.title: Saskatoon organizations show split opinions on proposed intersection design
item.description: After a report found 161 collisions in the past five years on 51st and Millar, the city is proposing a redesign of the intersection, but organizations are having mixed reactions.

item.title: Corrosion caused by road salt is taking a toll on Calgary’s fire trucks
item.description: The city of Calgary says it has spent $2 million this year to repair corrosion on the city's fire trucks believed caused by the road salts the city puts on its streets.

item.title: ‘I hear you’: Social disorder up, break-ins down, says Kelowna RCMP
item.description: Kelowna RCMP Supt. Chris Goebel addressed city council on Monday, acknowledging the day-to-day realities many businesses are facing.
